reference: GNU acl-utils setfacl in the reference Bash environment. Each parity case runs the same relative-path fixture script against GNU setfacl and the bash-os builtin; GNU status is checked before results are accepted, and stdout plus the fixture tree are compared. The tree snapshot records modes, contents, and links but not xattrs, so ACL effects are asserted where they change mode bits or affect a later operation.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata contract for the enabled builtin
Modification of owner, group-object, and other base permissions
Long-form modification across multiple relative files
End-of-options handling for a dash-prefixed relative filename
Continuation across a missing path, malformed ACL rejection, and symlink target behavior
Deferred named-entry, mask, and extended-entry operations that the current isolated environment cannot validate
exclusions: The fixture tree comparator does not include ACL xattr bytes or entries; runnable cases assert mode-visible behavior, while extended named-entry checks are deferred because both sides returned EINVAL in this environment.
Default ACLs, recursive operations, ACL text files, and resolution of real host users/groups are outside the documented builtin surface or the isolated fixture contract.

cases.purpose: Confirm through Bash builtins that setfacl is registered as an enabled builtin and has help metadata, without claiming GNU operation parity.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t setfacl) == builtin ]] || exit 1
help setfacl > metadata.out || exit 2
printf 'builtin\nhelp-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Apply the three base ACL entries to a new relative file and compare the resulting 0740 mode with GNU setfacl.
Set all three base ACL entries with --set and compare the resulting 0460 mode with GNU setfacl.
Use the long --modify form on two relative files and compare both base permission modes with GNU setfacl.
cases.script:
umask 077
: > first
: > second
setfacl --modify user::r--,group::r--,other::--- first second

cases.purpose: Apply a base permission change to a filename beginning with a dash after --, comparing GNU option termination behavior.
Pass a missing path before a valid file; require a diagnostic and verify both the failure status and that processing continues to update the later file.
cases.script:
umask 077
: > acl
if setfacl -m user::r-- missing acl; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
[[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Create a relative symlink and change its target's owner permissions; compare GNU's default symlink dereference behavior and the target mode.
cases.script:
umask 077
: > target
ln -s target alias
setfacl -m user::r-- alias

cases.purpose: Reject an invalid permission character, preserve the file, and compare the reported command status with GNU setfacl without pinning diagnostic wording.
cases.script:
umask 077
: > acl
if setfacl -m user:0:rwq acl; then exit 90; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Validate named entry creation, automatic and explicit masks, named-entry modification/removal, and -b removal followed by a base edit.
cases.reason: The reference GNU CLI and candidate both returned EINVAL while creating a named ACL in this isolated fixture environment, including with namespace-local numeric ID 0. A future run needs a disposable Linux VM with POSIX ACL xattr support and a distinct mapped UID/GID; only then can these extended ACL operations be compared.

cases.purpose: Repeated base-only ACL edits in one shell preserve each file state without needing named UID mappings.
cases.script:
umask 077
: > first
: > second
setfacl -m u::r-- first
setfacl --set u::rw-,g::---,o::--- second
setfacl -m g::r-- first
